players.product: AvalonMiner bitcoin mining machines (A15 / A16 series; Avalon A1566HA hydro-cooled)

quarterly_data.signal: CFO James Jin Cheng: Q2 2026 total revenue was approximately $32 million (CEO: below the previous guidance range of $35 million-$45 million; miner sales weakened noticeably from the second half of the quarter as Bitcoin prices fell). Product revenue was approximately $14 million; Canaan sold 2.5 exahash per second of computing power at an average selling price of $5.5 per terahash per second. Mining revenue was approximately $18 million with 243 Bitcoin mined, 55% of total revenue; excluding depreciation, the mining business gross margin was 20%. Adjusted EBITDA was a loss of $74.9 million, broadly in line with the previous quarter, including non-cash inventory write-downs, impairment of property, plant and equipment and fair value losses on digital assets.
quarterly_data.figure: Revenue ~$32M (guide was $35M-$45M); product ~$14M; 2.5 EH/s sold at $5.5/TH; mining ~$18M (55%), 243 BTC mined; mining gross margin ex-depreciation 20%; adjusted EBITDA loss $74.9M

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Nangeng Zhang and CFO: Canaan expects total revenues for the third quarter of 2026 to be between $11 million and $15 million. Although Bitcoin prices recovered somewhat at the end of August, miner procurement remains cautious, industry inventory still needs to be digested and some competitors have adopted a more aggressive pricing strategy to speed up cash collections; the company expects miner sales and average selling prices to remain under pressure in the third quarter and remains cautious about the near-term mining machine market (outlook reflects management's current judgment; actual results may differ).

CEO Nangeng Zhang: in Q2 hash price fluctuated between $0.028 and $0.039 per terahash per second per day; US capital markets and traditional mining companies continued to shift attention toward AI and HPC, and localized armed conflicts and tighter mining-related policies in China and elsewhere affected miners' investment willingness. Elevated industry inventory intensified price competition; Canaan adjusted pricing with more flexibility and emphasized production based on actual sales, controlling new production according to real orders; for existing machines it will evaluate whether to sell them to customers or deploy them in its own mining operations, based on cash collection, deployment conditions and additional investment requirements. Mining-rig demand outside the U.S. is also very weak, with no meaningful improvement yet. CEO: the company already holds mining machines and core parts in its own or its partner's inventory, 'maybe still at the wafer level', and can manufacture machines in a relatively short time for new sites.
quarterly_data.figure: Hash price $0.028-$0.039 per TH/s per day (Q2)

quarterly_data.signal: CFO James Jin Cheng: cash was $66 million at the end of Q2, up from $43 million at the end of Q1; Canaan collected $54 million in cash from product sales and used $35 million for operating expenses and working capital and $11 million for wafer purchases. Total operating expenses were $40 million including $9.2 million of impairment charges on property, plant and equipment and $2.7 million of credit losses; excluding these, operating expenses were $28.2 million, down 9% sequentially and 14% year-over-year, consistent with the build-to-order approach.
quarterly_data.figure: Cash $66M (from $43M); $11M wafer purchases; opex $40M ($28.2M ex-items, -9% QoQ, -14% YoY)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Nangeng Zhang: Canaan adjusted its deployed hash rate in Q2 based on power prices, load management and site conditions; mining revenues accounted for more than 50% of total revenue and continued to cover direct operating costs such as power and hosting. As of the end of June installed hash rate in non-JV projects was approximately 10.05 exahash per second, and the average all-in power cost in June was about $0.043 per kilowatt hour.
quarterly_data.figure: ~10.05 EH/s installed (non-JV, end of June); ~$0.043/kWh all-in power cost (June)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO and CFO: at the end of the second quarter Canaan held 1,915 Bitcoin and 3,952 Ethereum, worth $112 million at carrying value as of June 30 (a record digital-assets treasury). In late August, authorized by its board, Canaan sold all its Ethereum holdings and 54 Bitcoins, generating approximately $13.9 million in cash.
quarterly_data.figure: 1,915 BTC and 3,952 ETH held ($112M carrying value, June 30); sold all ETH and 54 BTC for ~$13.9M (late August)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO and CFO on Project ABC (partner WindHQ, which runs site operations and power management while Canaan supplies mining machines and technology): Canaan and its partner continued the mining machine upgrade in Q2; the project generated positive cash flow, and installed hashrate reached 4.85 exahash per second at the end of July, up 10% from the end of March. Canaan received $5.2 million in cash from Project ABC in Q2, including sales collections and cash distributions, and cumulative cash received reached $8.4 million as of August 31; retirement of older mining machines caused a one-time loss, so Canaan recognized approximately $4 million of equity investment losses for Project ABC in Q2. CFO: no other deal like Project ABC has been closed yet, but some projects are under discussion, with expansion focused on North America, especially the U.S.
quarterly_data.figure: 4.85 EH/s at Project ABC (end of July, +10% from end of March); $5.2M cash received in Q2, $8.4M cumulative (August 31); ~$4M equity investment loss
quarterly_data.counterparty_role: Project ABC partner (site operations and power management)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Nangeng Zhang on product generations: the older Avalon A15 machines run at 15.8 to 17.8 joules per terahash; the A16 series (cost-effective air-cooled and high-temperature HydroCool models, advanced in Q2) runs at 12.8 to 16.8 joules per terahash. Canaan plans to deploy at least part of the A16 machines in its own mining fleet next year and assumes it will upgrade 70% of its machines to the more advanced, cost-effective models next year.
quarterly_data.figure: A15 15.8-17.8 J/TH; A16 12.8-16.8 J/TH; 70% of own fleet to be upgraded next year (assumption)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Nangeng Zhang: the Avalon Home consumer line (home heating miners) generated approximately $1 million in revenue in Q2 and sales came down after the heating season ended; Q2 was devoted to R&D on new Avalon Home products, which Canaan is preparing for mass production in the third quarter, and it plans to launch new products and updates during the Christmas shopping season, aiming at the northern-hemisphere winter heating season. Too early to give a revenue-mix target.
quarterly_data.figure: Avalon Home ~$1 million revenue (Q2); mass production prep in Q3; launch in Christmas shopping season

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Nangeng Zhang on compute-to-heat: the earlier Nordic project has validated the feasibility of using HydroCool equipment for district heating (high-temperature HydroCool equipment can supply the hot water needed for heating); the Nordic heating projects already have 2 MW of equipment in operation and a customer ordered another 6 MW in March this year. The market is still early and small scale and does not yet indicate a broader demand recovery outside the U.S.
quarterly_data.figure: 2 MW in operation; 6 MW additional order (March this year)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Nangeng Zhang: Canaan is advancing several long-term power resource projects in North America and its confidence in securing gigawatt-scale load by the end of 2026 remains intact; it will not yet disclose sites, capacities or stages. It is too early to choose between co-location and GPU cloud rental for HPC; Canaan will not build end-to-end AI HPC data centers by itself, since that may exceed its capital capabilities, and will work with capital providers, engineering contractors and other partners; no specific partnership agreements can be disclosed. CFO: Canaan is paying some cash as deposits to secure power / HPC data-center opportunities, its mining-machine inventory can be injected into new mining projects as capex without cash, and securing gigawatt-level power comes first.
quarterly_data.figure: Gigawatt-scale load targeted by end of 2026

quarterly_data.signal: CFO James Jin Cheng named 'Cipher Mining, Cipher Digital or WindHQ' as partners in Project ABC (where Canaan is upgrading the mining machine fleet) that 'supported us' and 'do good deals with us in a transparent way, in a fair way'.
